title: The camera is not blocked by trees. It is under a deck that does not exist to the collision system — and one absence produces three false negatives at once.
roadmap_item: G1, and it hands work to W4/W5
the_measurement: RI-CAM01 §C.1's automatic fail is NOT cleared. Against the shipped build: a CLOSED run of 26 consecutive `player_occluded` frames (sim 285-310) against a bar of <= 6. Mean 0.65 against a bar of 0.03. At 60 Hz that is 0.43 s, where the item's own rationale is that anything past 0.1 s hides a roll's i-frame window. The run begins and ends inside the measured frames, so 26 is a complete measurement and not a window-truncated lower bound — a wider window can only make it worse.
the_finding_that_relocates_the_problem: THE PLAYER IS UNDER A RAISED DECK IN LILMOTH, AND THAT DECK IS NOT IN `plan.buildings` — nearest entry is 13.9 m away — so it never becomes a `settlementSolids()` collision box. ONE ABSENCE PRODUCES THREE FALSE NEGATIVES SIMULTANEOUSLY: (1) the spring arm reports `armHit: false` on every frame with `armLen` pinned at 3.993 m, because a thing that is not in the collider set cannot be hit; (2) the §D `clip_through` detector reads false even on frames where the camera is inside the slab, because §D is defined against that same collision set; and (3) the occluder fade never fires, because it is canopy-only. Three instruments agreeing that nothing is wrong, all of them reading the same empty set.
why_this_matters_beyond_the_camera: This is the same shape as the diagnosis a previous round reached about trees — `InstancedMesh` canopy was never wired into any `CollisionCell`, so the arm was working exactly as designed against a set a tree could not be a member of. That was fixed for vegetation. THE SAME HOLE EXISTS FOR ARCHITECTURE, and architecture is worse: a deck, a balcony, an overhang or a stair underside is exactly the geometry a third-person camera collides with in a town. THE NEXT PIECE IS THIN OR ABSENT ARCHITECTURE IN THE COLLISION SET, NOT MORE VEGETATION WORK.
the_fix_that_landed_is_real_but_orthogon: Commit b476b55d's camera-to-actor sightline test works and is live in this region (Lilmoth is `western-rootlands`, canopy radius 4.5 m, well past the ~1.06 m threshold below which the segment test can never beat the old proximity bubble). Both arms were byte-identical on every frame here — not because the fix is inert, but because the occluder is not a tree. The control was proved non-inert by construction rather than by the arms differing: `occlusion-sightline-check.mjs` Arm A reports proximity-only VISIBLE and with-sightline hidden. That is rule 6 done properly on a case where the arms legitimately agree.
four_instrument_defects_found_in_a_tool_: THE REFERENCE ARM RECORDED AN IMPOSSIBLE NUMBER AND NOBODY READ IT. The predecessor's probe carries `occludedPx 2568` against `refPx 161` — a ratio of 15.95, i.e. more occluded pixels than the player has — from sampling the reference at frame 0 before the scene settled and carrying it forward. Silently, that scores frames `occluded: false`. IT MANUFACTURES A PASS. Fixed with warm-up plus a guard scoring such frames null.

The manifest was written only at completion, so an aborted walk lost 100% of its frames. Two runs died mid-walk — the predecessor's, and this one's, killed at elapsed 123 s by HAZARDS §10's fleet-wide `pkill` signature. Now per-frame JSONL plus a partial manifest on abort.
Frame labels drifted 5 frames from sim frames the moment a warm-up was added. Now read from `sim.frame`.

Added §15's per-frame liveness gate (0 non-LIVE) and §16's motion proof (1.92 m travelled, 36/36 frames moved), after verifying `queueInputs`/`stepFrames` actually exist and that the harness call dies loudly rather than swallowing.
a_deviation_the_successor_must_know: The colour-diff proxy standing in for an ID buffer reads 0.53 on a PROVABLY UNOCCLUDED player, not 1.0 — so it is biased toward declaring occlusion. It does not threaten this result (the run frames fall to 34 px of 595, far past any bias) but it would threaten a marginal one. Do not reuse it for a close call without fixing it.
ri_cam04_is_not_judgeable_and_that_is_th: Not a zero against the build: `roll_bin` is untraced (0 hits) and EIGHT OF ITS NINE directional roll clips are absent from `game/data/`. That is corpus and content debt. The agent verified this with its own greps rather than inheriting the method script's claims. RI-CAM03 needs ~25,200 locked frames for M1 alone and its required `onScreen(eid)` harness method does not exist — that is a round of its own, not a follow-on.
still_owed: RI-CAM01's blind pair has never run. Per CLAUDE.md rule 0e only the orchestrator can spawn the judge, and it caps the item independently of §C.1 no matter what the measurement says.
someone_is_still_running_pkill: This agent's browsers were killed mid-run at elapsed 123 s by a fleet-wide `pkill -f headless_shell`. HAZARDS §10 has forbidden that since yesterday, with three siblings' captures lost to it. It is still happening. Kill by PID only.
next_step: Dispatch: put thin and absent architecture into the collision set — decks, balconies, overhangs, stair undersides — and re-measure RI-CAM01 §C.1 against it. Acceptance: the longest closed run of `player_occluded` frames falls to <= 6 at the Lilmoth stand, with the deck present in the collider set and `armHit` true on frames where the camera is inside it. Then run RI-CAM01's blind pair.
